t: The Thuận Hóa region passed from Champa to Đại Việt in 1306, and from the late 16th century the Nguyễn lords governed it and based themselves at Phú Xuân in 1687.
Phú Xuân was the capital of Đàng Trong from 1738 to 1775, fell to the Trịnh lords in 1775 and to the Tây Sơn in 1786, and was retaken in 1802 by Nguyễn Ánh, who made it the capital of all Vietnam.
It was renamed Huế in 1899 under the French, remained the seat of the Nguyễn emperors until Bảo Đại abdicated in 1945, and became a centrally governed city in 2025.
dyk: The first written use of the name Huế may be a line of a Chữ Nôm poem attributed to Emperor Lê Thánh Tông that mentions "Huế rice"; older documents called the place Phú Xuân, Kinh Đô or simply Kinh.
ev: The oldest ruins in the area, those of the Kingdom of Lâm Ấp, date from this time
Champa cedes the Ô and Lý prefectures to Đại Việt, which renames them Thuận and Hóa
The Nguyễn lords base their operations at Phú Xuân
Phú Xuân becomes the capital of Đàng Trong
Nguyễn Ánh retakes Phú Xuân, rebuilds the citadel and makes it the capital of all Vietnam
Phú Xuân is officially renamed Huế under French rule
Emperor Bảo Đại abdicates and the capital moves to Hanoi
North Vietnamese and Việt Cộng forces occupy most of Huế in the Tết Offensive; the city is retaken after a month of fighting

f.founded: The oldest ruins in the area belong to the Kingdom of Lâm Ấp and date to the 4th century CE; the Nguyễn lords based themselves at Phú Xuân in 1687, and Nguyễn Ánh made it the imperial capital after 1802.
f.where: On the Perfume River (Sông Hương) in central Vietnam, between mountains, hills, plains and a coastal lagoon, bordering Quảng Trị to the north, Đà Nẵng to the south, Laos to the west and the South China Sea to the east.
f.known: The Cham ruins of Kandarpapura; Thuận Hóa, ceded to Đại Việt in 1306; Phú Xuân, capital of the Nguyễn lords; the capital of Vietnam under the Nguyễn dynasty, 1802 to 1945; the Imperial City and imperial tombs; the áo dài; Buddhist monasteries and Huế cuisine
f.today: Huế is one of Vietnam's centrally governed cities, and since 2025 it has included the whole of the former Thừa Thiên Huế province.
